checks: Matched source ed1a79b6ef1fd236 §§1, 3–4, (1)–(3), and checked the local argument from §2. The sharper count assumes both null overlaps and no full trace on any maximal-dimensional fiber.

Compactness gives finitely many integer fibers. Their largest affine dimension is q, and the lower-dimensional ones have zero H_q mass. The almost-everywhere partition and null overlaps restrict to each positive intrinsic fiber. A point missed by finitely many closed caps has a relatively open missed neighborhood of positive intrinsic volume.

Local incidence one and the exclusion of whole-fiber traces give one opposite pair meeting the intrinsic interior on its common cutting hyperplane. Any third positive trace overlaps the pair on positive measure. At a common cut mark every other margin is strictly negative: a vanishing margin would either cut a positive side or vanish on the entire intrinsic plane.

For a same-parity pair, the actual integer midpoint fiber contains the Minkowski average. Its direction space contains the sum of the two source directions and has dimension at most q, so all three directions coincide. An average of two intrinsic interior cut marks has an intrinsic ball at the midpoint. Only shared labels can survive at that point, and just one shared proper label would leave an open half-ball uncovered. Both labels have positive traces there and therefore give the midpoint label pair.

Each positive-mass cap appears at some positive fiber, so at most 2c(P) labels occur. Every occupied parity maps to one component. When c(P)=k the map is bijective, so each component is one parity and closed under pairwise midpoints. A closest distinct pair contradicts that closure and finiteness. Equal masses give M=rD, and the binomial bound (1+1/q)^q>=2 gives the stated Gamma_q comparison, including q=1.
